description: Schema definition used to create the Poutine Submission table (layer 3/9 of the Poutine League Dataverse data model build-out). Source of truth: ARCHITECTURE.md §1 (Data model), POUTINE_SUBMISSION entity block. Most complex layer so far: real lookups to Restaurant (layer 1) and systemuser (built-in), plus an N:N relationship to Tag (layer 2).

table.purpose: A submitted poutine, owned by the submitting employee. Central fact table linking a Restaurant, a submitting systemuser, and a set of Tags.

columns.notes: Primary name column (poutine name), auto-created with the table.

Created via an IntEnum (PoutineSubmissionStatus) passed to client.tables.add_columns(). The 'In Review' label (a display name with a space, invalid as a Python identifier) was supplied via the enum's __labels__ dunder class attribute, which the SDK reads for custom multi-word display labels and Python's Enum metaclass ignores as machinery.

Chose true Currency (MoneyAttributeMetadata) over Decimal: a menu price is semantically a monetary amount, and Dataverse Currency columns get built-in currency-aware formatting/base-currency conversion (rpo_price_base). The SDK's add_columns() 'decimal'/'money' type strings both map to DecimalAttributeMetadata, not true Money -- required a raw Web API POST to EntityDefinitions(...)/Attributes with @odata.type Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.MoneyAttributeMetadata.

Dataverse Image column (ImageAttributeMetadata) -- not exposed by the SDK's add_columns() type strings ('file' maps to FileAttributeMetadata, a generic file column, not Image). Created via raw Web API POST. Left null for all sample data per task scope (no need to source real images for this layer).

lookups.creationMethod: client.tables.create_lookup_field() -- worked as-is because the referenced table (rpo_restaurant) already carries the rpo customization prefix, so the SDK's auto-generated relationship schema name is valid.

client.tables.create_lookup_field() FAILED here: its auto-generated relationship schema name is '{referenced}_{referencing}_{lookupField}', which for systemuser (a built-in table with no customization prefix) produces 'systemuser_rpo_poutinesubmission_rpo_SubmitterId' -- rejected by Dataverse because custom EntityRelationship schema names must themselves start with a valid customization prefix. Worked around by calling client.tables.create_one_to_many_relationship() directly with LookupAttributeMetadata + OneToManyRelationshipMetadata, supplying an explicit rpo_-prefixed relationship schema name ('rpo_PoutineSubmission_Submitter'). This is a reusable pattern for any future lookup to a built-in/OOB Dataverse table.

solutionAttachment.issue: As with layers 1 & 2, client.tables.create()/add_columns()/create_lookup_field()/create_many_to_many_relationship() calls passed solution="poutineleaguecore" but the table's own Entity component did not reliably show up via a plain solutioncomponent query at first read.
solutionAttachment.remediation: pac solution add-solution-component --solutionUniqueName poutineleaguecore --component <GUID> --componentType 1 --environment <env> for the table (schema-name form failed with 'Failed to resolve entity metadata'; the EntityMetadataId GUID had to be used). For the three relationships (Restaurant lookup, Submitter lookup, Tag N:N) the same command was run with --componentType 10 (Entity Relationship) and each relationship's relationship_id GUID.
solutionAttachment.verificationMethod: Queried solutioncomponent for componenttype=1 (table present) and confirmed the table's RootComponentBehavior is 'Include Subcomponents' (0). Then did a scratch pac solution export + unpack (not committed) and grepped the resulting customizations.xml for all three EntityRelationship schema names -- all three (rpo_restaurant_rpo_poutinesubmission_rpo_RestaurantId, rpo_PoutineSubmission_Submitter, rpo_PoutineSubmission_Tag) were present, confirming relationships attached to an entity with 'Include Subcomponents' export correctly even when a direct solutioncomponent row for componenttype=10 isn't independently listed (Dataverse treats them as implied subcomponents once the parent entity is included with that behavior).

creationMethod.tool: PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client (Python SDK) with raw Web API fallback for Money and Image column types, and for the systemuser relationship schema name.
creationMethod.phasedCreation: Table + Description/Status columns first, then Price/Photo (Web API), then Restaurant + Submitter lookups, then the Tag N:N relationship -- each phase separated by a 20-25s wait for metadata propagation per the dv-metadata skill's phased-creation guidance.
creationMethod.notes: Table creation followed by an immediate list_columns() call transiently returned 'Table not found' even though client.tables.get() succeeded -- actual propagation lag in this environment was closer to 50-55s total, longer than the skill's suggested 15-30s baseline.
